strategy: Wave-based scoped closure with runtime authority decided first, data-layer closure second, gate migration third, and final acceptance last.

conflicts.description: Desktop runtime already prefers Node, but build-time default still routes to Python when NIKO_GATEWAY_RUNTIME is unset.
conflicts.strategy: Make Node the authoritative default in desktop build scripts before touching release gates.
conflicts.impact: desktop scripts, packaging docs, sidecar validation flow

conflicts.description: Python utility scripts and README still point to missing src runtime modules, causing release and delivery commands to fail in the current checkout.
conflicts.strategy: Either restore a bounded Python fallback path or explicitly retire those references and replace them with TypeScript authority.
conflicts.impact: build scripts, operational docs, local release commands

conflicts.description: Focused Phase 4 suites pass, but the official aggregate test:phase4 command still exits non-zero.
conflicts.strategy: Close the remaining data-layer tail first, then stabilize the official aggregate command and coverage path.
conflicts.impact: migration verification confidence, CI and release quality signal

conflicts.description: Some compatibility layers were intentionally kept during migration, but they need explicit retention or removal decisions before closure.
conflicts.strategy: Treat desktop and MCP contract consumers as hard boundaries, then prune or document the remaining shims.

accepted_resolutions: Use four dependency waves with low-overlap scopes.
Move release and delivery gate migration after build authority and Phase 4 baseline stabilization.
Keep external adapter expansion and non-core product polish out of scope for this closure plan.
Produce both workflow-plan artifacts and a CSV wave session so execution can start without re-planning.
